cells.tense: Right now you stand alongside something still growing and read it honestly as it changes.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Name the part of what you tend that is finished, set it down this week, and put your hands back on the part still growing. Keep both halves — the clearing and the feeding.
cells.core: You are tending something unfinished, and your read on it is clear. You see what is actually there, not what you hope for, and you let it keep going. What is not good for it gets named and set down; what serves it gets fed. That is not calculation. It is care with open eyes, and the ones being tended feel the evenness in it — nobody asked to be more than they can be yet. Some of what you carry has already given what it had. The hours spent holding the finished parts are hours the growing part does not get. This week, let a finished piece end, then give the returned time to what is still young. Both halves of that are one act.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what is growing with eyes that tell the truth.
cells.verb: holding fair ground for something still becoming
cells.place: at the side of what is young and growing

cells.tense: Your care is running ahead of what you tend, braced against outcomes not yet here.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Hold one growing thing this week without a single push toward what you want it to become. Stand by it as it is. If the urge to correct it comes, wait a day first.
cells.core: Your hand is already on the future of what you tend. You know what it should become, and each small thing it does gets measured against that shape. The caring is honest, and it has a grip in it — people can feel the expectation, and the thing itself slows under the weight of being aimed. A builder's strength is in the standing-by, not the squeeze. You have held heavy things without crushing them before. This week, hold one growing thing exactly as it is. Do not correct it toward what it could be. If the urge to push comes, wait a day and see whether it stays. Some of it will not.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying it, and your grip is doing the work.
cells.verb: holding fair ground for something still becoming
cells.place: at the side of what is young and growing

cells.tense: Something was growing and you are still standing at a door you already walked through.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Take something you are tending and put its actual history on paper, in plain order, dates if you have them, no feeling words. Then read it once. Nothing has to follow.
cells.core: Something is being tended and you are not there for it. Not because the caring stopped — because you are still in an earlier moment, and it has moved on without you. What you offer arrives late, or arrives as memory, and there is a distance between you and what is actually beside you. Coming back starts on paper. Take something you are tending and put its history on paper, one line at a time, in order, no feeling words. When the account is down, read it once. That is all that is asked. Anything further, if it comes, will come from seeing the thing clearly instead of from where you left it.
cells.sheetLine: You are still at a door that is already behind you.
cells.verb: holding fair ground for something still becoming
cells.place: at the side of what is young and growing

cells.tense: The even hand you put on this is yours, and you call it just how it goes.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: Next time you steady something you are tending, wait long enough to recognize that you are the one doing it. Let that be enough — no plan after. One moment, then back to the work.
cells.core: You are tending something and you keep making it fair. You step in when one part gets too much, hold back when another needs room, say the level thing when the room goes loud. Asked, you would say that is what anyone would do. But not many do, and the way you do it has a stamp on it. You can tell what something needs before you could explain how. That knowing is not borrowed from anywhere. It is yours. This week, before you even the ground under something, wait long enough to recognize that you are the one evening it. Stay in that moment, then do it or do not. Nothing needs to come of it. It only needs to be seen.
cells.sheetLine: You say it is how it goes, and the hand is yours.
cells.verb: holding fair ground for something still becoming
cells.place: at the side of what is young and growing
